contentObjective: I can explain a percent as a rate per 100, model it on a decimal grid or tape diagram, and interpret percents greater than 100%.

examples.text: 65 shaded squares out of a 100-square grid is 65%

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Car Sales
revealWordProblem.text:
A car dealership's sales for one month are shown in the monthly sales report. The owner now needs to order 50 cars from the factory.
Question: Based on the sales shown, how many of each type of car do you recommend the owner order?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A monthly sales report bar graph out of 100 cars sold: 8 hybrid, 18 all-electric, and 74 gas-powered.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Out of 100 cars sold, 8 were hybrid, 18 were all-electric, and 74 were gas-powered, so those counts are already percents: 8%, 18%, and 74%. Apply each percent to the 50-car order: 8% of 50 = 4 hybrids, 18% of 50 = 9 all-electric, and 74% of 50 = 37 gas-powered. That accounts for all 50 cars (4 + 9 + 37 = 50), so I recommend ordering 4, 9, and 37.

questions.stem: What does the word percent mean?
questions.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
choiceFeedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
Percent = per 100.
questions.explanationEs: Por ciento significa por cada cien, y por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como una fracción con denominador 100.
hintsEs: Mira la segunda parte de la palabra: ciento.
Un siglo son 100 años; un centavo es 1/100 de dólar.

questions.stem: 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
questions.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
choiceFeedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.
questions.stemEs: 3 de cada 10 estudiantes caminan a la escuela. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos términos de la razón por 10 para compararla con 100: 3 de 10 se convierte en 30 de 100, o sea 30%.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje compara con 100, así que reescribe la razón sobre 100.
Multiplica AMBOS términos por ese mismo número.

questions.stem: A decimal grid has 100 squares and 65 are shaded. What percent is shaded?
questions.explanation: Each square is one percent, so 65 shaded squares is 65%.
choiceFeedback: 35 is the number of UNshaded squares.
65 out of 100 is 65%, not 6.5%.
100% would mean every square is shaded.
hints: How many squares are in the whole grid?
Each square stands for 1%.
Count the shaded squares.
questions.stemEs: Una cuadrícula decimal tiene 100 cuadros y 65 están sombreados. ¿Qué porcentaje está sombreado?
questions.explanationEs: Cada cuadro es un por ciento, así que 65 cuadros sombreados son 65%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos cuadros hay en toda la cuadrícula?

reviewHighlights.formula: Percent = Parts per 100 = Ratio of a number to 100
steps: 3. Fraction to Percent: Scale fraction to a denominator of 100
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake with percent is scaling only one term of the ratio: reading 7 out of 10 as 7%. A percent compares to 100, so BOTH terms must be multiplied by the same factor — 10 × 10 = 100, so 7 × 10 = 70, giving 70%. Reading it as 7% describes seats that are nearly empty when they are nearly full. A second mistake is treating a percent as an amount: 150% of a 200-point goal is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points, not 150 points.

level1.stem: Which percent means MORE than one whole?
level1.explanation: 100% is exactly one whole, so any percent above 100 is more than one whole.
choiceFeedback: 100% is exactly one whole, not more.
80% is less than one whole.
0.8% is a tiny sliver of one whole.
hints: What percent stands for one whole?
Anything above that is more than the whole.
Compare each choice to 100.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál porcentaje significa MÁS de un entero?
level1.explanationEs: 100% es exactamente un entero, así que cualquier porcentaje mayor que 100 es más de un entero.
hintsEs: Todo lo que esté por encima de eso es más que el entero.

level1.stem: Sort each percent by how it compares to one whole.
level1.explanation: 100% is the dividing line: it means exactly one whole. Everything below is part of a whole; everything above is more than a whole.
hints: What percent equals one whole?
Compare each number to 100.
99% is just under; 101% is just over.
level1.stemEs: Clasifica cada porcentaje según cómo se compara con un entero.
level1.explanationEs: 100% es la línea divisoria: significa exactamente un entero. Todo lo que está por debajo es parte de un entero; todo lo que está por encima es más de un entero.
hintsEs: 99% queda justo por debajo; 101% queda justo por encima.

level1.stem: Match each comparison to its percent.
level1.explanation: Every percent is a ratio rewritten with 100 as the second term. The whole is always 100%.
hints: Rewrite each comparison out of 100.
1.5 wholes is one whole plus half a whole.
The whole itself is 100%.
level1.stemEs: Relaciona cada comparación con su porcentaje.
level1.explanationEs: Todo porcentaje es una razón reescrita con 100 como segundo término. El entero siempre es 100%.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.2) A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Double-check your division: $4.50 ÷ 9 — is it $0.45 or $0.50?
Divide the cost by the number of games: $4.50 ÷ 9, not some other operation.
That's the total cost for all 9 games, not the cost for one game.
hints: You know the total cost ($4.50) and the total games (9). A unit rate tells the cost of just ONE game.
To find a unit rate, divide the total cost by the number of games so the second quantity becomes 1.
Set up the division: $4.50 ÷ 9. Think of $4.50 as 450 cents if that makes the division easier.
level1.stemEs: Un puesto cobra $4.50 por 9 juegos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: Conoces el costo total ($4.50) y el total de juegos (9). Una tasa unitaria dice el costo de UN solo juego.
Para hallar una tasa unitaria, divide el costo total entre el número de juegos para que la segunda cantidad sea 1.
Plantea la división: $4.50 ÷ 9. Piensa en $4.50 como 450 centavos si eso te facilita la división.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.2) A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
choiceFeedback: That's the number of gallons — you need to divide 180 by 6, not use 6 as the answer.
That's the total miles — divide 180 by 6 to find miles for one gallon.
Check your division: 180 ÷ 6 — is it 30 or 36?
hints: Notice the units in the question: miles PER gallon. That tells you miles go on top and gallons on the bottom.
Divide the total miles by the total gallons so you get the miles for just 1 gallon.
Start the division: 180 ÷ 6. Think: 6 × what number lands on 180?
level1.stemEs: Un carro recorre 180 millas usando 6 galones de gasolina. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en millas por galón?
hintsEs: Fíjate en las unidades de la pregunta: millas POR galón. Eso te dice que las millas van arriba y los galones abajo.
Divide el total de millas entre el total de galones para obtener las millas de 1 solo galón.
Empieza la división: 180 ÷ 6. Piensa: 6 × ¿qué número da 180?

1.5% is a tiny sliver — but the orange kitten is heavier.
hints: Which kitten is the whole?

level2.stemEs: El gatito anaranjado pesa 1.5 veces lo que pesa el gatito gris. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito gris es eso?

hintsEs: Un entero es 100%. ¿Cuánto es medio entero?

level3.stem: A car dealership sold 50 cars last month: 20 sedans, 15 SUVs, 10 trucks, and 5 vans. The owner will order 100 cars for next month and wants the order to match last month's sales pattern. Write each type as a percent, then say how many of each to order — and explain why percents make this easier than the raw counts.
level3.sampleAnswer: Each count is out of 50, so multiply both terms by 2 to compare to 100: sedans 20/50 = 40/100 = 40%, SUVs 15/50 = 30/100 = 30%, trucks 10/50 = 20/100 = 20%, vans 5/50 = 10/100 = 10%. The percents total 100%, which confirms the whole is accounted for. Because the new order is exactly 100 cars, each percent IS the number to order: 40 sedans, 30 SUVs, 20 trucks, and 10 vans. Percents make this easier because they restate every count against the same whole of 100, so two months with different totals can be compared directly.
hints: Each sale count is out of 50 — rewrite each one out of 100.
What do you multiply 50 by to get 100?
Check that your four percents add to 100%.

Escribe cada tipo como porcentaje, luego di cuántos pedir de cada uno — y explica por qué los porcentajes lo hacen más fácil que las cantidades originales.
hintsEs: Cada conteo de ventas es sobre 50 — reescribe cada uno sobre 100.

level3.stem: In Mr. Alvarez's class 40% of 30 students play an instrument. In the chess club 60% of 15 members do. Which group has MORE musicians?
choices: The chess club, because 60% is greater than 40%
They tie, because both are close to half
You cannot compare percents of different-sized groups
level3.explanation: A percent is a rate per 100 of something, and the somethings differ here. 40% of 30 is 12; 60% of 15 is 9. The bigger percent sits on the smaller whole, so it produces fewer people — 12 beats 9.
choiceFeedback: 60% is the larger rate, but it is taken of 15 rather than 30. Work out both counts.
12 and 9 are not a tie.
You can compare them — convert each percent into a number of people first.
hints: A percent on its own is not a count. Per 100 of what?
Find 40% of 30, then 60% of 15.
Compare the two counts, not the two percents.
level3.stemEs: En la clase del Sr. Alvarez, el 40% de 30 estudiantes toca un instrumento. En el club de ajedrez lo hace el 60% de 15 miembros. ¿Qué grupo tiene MÁS músicos?
choicesEs: El club de ajedrez, porque 60% es mayor que 40%
Empatan, porque ambos están cerca de la mitad
No se pueden comparar porcentajes de grupos de distinto tamaño
level3.explanationEs: Un porcentaje es una tasa por 100 de algo, y aquí los algos son distintos. El 40% de 30 es 12; el 60% de 15 es 9. El porcentaje mayor está sobre el total menor, así que da menos personas — 12 supera a 9.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje por sí solo no es un conteo. ¿Por 100 de qué?
Calcula el 40% de 30 y luego el 60% de 15.
Compara los dos conteos, no los dos porcentajes.

tool.title: One whole vs. 400% of it
tool.caption: The top bar is one whole (100% = 15 points). The bottom bar stacks four of those wholes, so 400% = 60 points — four times the whole, not part of it.
